answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a wander as the anchor of the cost.
